calls.head: Strength against strength
calls.body: The Canadiens are one of the league’s best for chance quality, and the Maple Leafs are near the top of the league at preventing dangerous shots. Our lean: the Canadiens’ chance quality wins out.
calls.call: The Canadiens’ chances are more dangerous than the league average (a 6.3% chance of scoring on the average shot) against the Maple Leafs.
calls.nums: Montréal 2nd for chance quality (a 6.8% chance of scoring on the average shot) · Toronto 8th for preventing dangerous shots
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 0 and 0 games this season
calls.happened: On chance quality, Montréal had 7.6% a shot. The league average is 6.3% a shot, and they came in at 6.8% a shot.

calls.head: The Canadiens lock it down; the Maple Leafs don’t
calls.body: The Canadiens are around the middle of the league for shot suppression, at the stingy end; the Maple Leafs are the league’s worst, at the porous end. Expect that gap to show.
calls.call: The Canadiens allow fewer 5-on-5 shot attempts per 60 than the Maple Leafs.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 0 and 0 games this season
calls.happened: On 5-on-5 shot attempts allowed per 60, Montréal had 48.0 per 60 and Toronto 53.9 per 60. Coming in, Montréal was at 57.3 per 60 and Toronto at 63.6 per 60.

TOR.head: We gave Toronto only a 34% chance, and it went the way we feared.

MTL.head: We gave Montréal a 66% chance, and Montréal delivered.

surprises.head: Montréal tried a different line
surprises.body: C. Caufield, C. Kreider, N. Suzuki played 10:28 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of Montréal’s usual lines.

story.head: The Canadiens beat the Maple Leafs
paras: William Nylander opened the scoring 48 seconds in. Alexandre Carrier scored the winner midway through the third.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. By our Swing measure, Josh Anderson had the best night of anyone. The Canadiens tried a line they hadn’t used before: Cole Caufield, Chris Kreider and Nick Suzuki.

items.text: Whether the Canadiens keep that line together in Pittsburgh on Saturday.
Both of the preview’s calls held.
